angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 310,978 km at 37.68 pc = 0.11 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 26.5393 +/- 0.0230 mas (same row, RUWE 1.53): 37.68 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.447 +/- 0.013 solar radii from Stassun et al. (2019), AJ 158, 138 (TIC v8.2), the mass of TIC 29960109 (VizieR IV/39/tic82) (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/ab3467); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3450 +/- 157 K from Stassun et al. (2019), AJ 158, 138 (TIC v8.2), the effective temperature of TIC 29960109 (VizieR IV/39/tic82) (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/ab3467). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
